title: Cap cards "view all" link uses the primary link style
detail: The link under the cap cards no longer renders in muted grey; it uses the default link variant like other text links.

title: Cap amounts follow their unit and a limit of 0 reads "Not included"
detail: Values with unit "mb" show as MB, GB or TB (base 1024), count and tokens use the locale's digit grouping. A limit of 0 or less shows "Not included" instead of a 0 bar, also when nothing is measured. caps:usage rows and the tenant-caps list cells now carry the unit of the cap. New key cap-overview.notIncluded in all locale packages.

title: CapCardsPanel can be limited to specific cap keys via params.capKeys
detail: A custom dashboard panel with params capKeys as a list of cap ids shows only those cards, in the order of the capsUsage query. Anything other than a list of strings means no limit, and capKeys is not sent to the server. Each limited cap card also shows how much is left (or that nothing is), next to the percent chip, and a limited panel adds a link to the full usage screen.

title: Tenant caps list decrypts only the visible page
detail: Without a search and with a sort other than name, the list loads light tenant rows, pages them, and fetches and decrypts names for the current page only. The default name sort and any search still decrypt every tenant, because tenant names are stored encrypted and cannot be sorted or filtered in SQL. Order, total and rows are unchanged.

title: tenant-caps:list pages by offset and rejects cursor
detail: The cap overview list showed page 1 on every page because the pager sends offset and the query only read cursor. tenant-caps:list now takes offset like the pager; a cursor in the payload is rejected with a 400 validation error and sort is an enum of the sortable fields. The unused cap-overview.errors.invalidCursor and sortFieldUnsupported keys are gone.
migration: Callers of cap-overview:query:tenant-caps:list must send offset instead of cursor, and only a sortable field name as sort. Apps that override the removed i18n keys cap-overview.errors.invalidCursor or cap-overview.errors.sortFieldUnsupported can delete them. No caller in the kumiko-enterprise, kumiko-platform, kumiko-studio or app repos sends a cursor or defines these keys.

title: Cap overview lists no destroyed tenants
detail: tenant-options and tenant-caps-list now filter destroyed tenants and keep reading tenant names through the PII-aware path.

title: caps:usage and my-caps default to admin roles; widen with usageVisibleTo
detail: `createCapOverviewFeature` gets `usageVisibleTo?: readonly string[]`. Without it, the `caps:usage` query and the `my-caps` screen accept `access.admin` (TenantAdmin, Admin, SystemAdmin) instead of every tenant member. The screen and the query share the resolved roles. Only built-in roles are accepted (User, Member, Editor, Admin, TenantAdmin, SystemAdmin); an unknown or empty list throws at feature definition. The SystemAdmin `tenantId` override and the platform-wide screens are unchanged. The `MY_CAPS_ACCESS_ROLES` export is replaced by `DEFAULT_CAP_USAGE_ROLES` (the admin default), and `myCapsScreen` by `createMyCapsScreen(roles)`.
migration: Apps whose regular members should keep seeing their usage pass `createCapOverviewFeature({ ..., usageVisibleTo: ["User", "Editor", "Admin", "TenantAdmin", "SystemAdmin"] })`. Code that imported `MY_CAPS_ACCESS_ROLES` (handlers or nav entries mirroring the screen rule) imports `DEFAULT_CAP_USAGE_ROLES` for the admin default, or reuses the same `usageVisibleTo` array it passed to the feature.

title: Cross-tenant cap limits read the target tenant's config
detail: `caps:usage` with a SystemAdmin `tenantId` override and `tenant-caps:list` passed the caller's config accessor to `CapSpec.limit`, so a limit that reads a tenant-scoped config key showed the caller's value for every tenant. Both now resolve one accessor per target tenant through `ctx.configFor`, and `tenant-caps:list` resolves each tenant's limit separately instead of once per tier.

title: tenant-caps:list validates cursor and filters, parallel usage reads; cap-counter list not searchable
detail: `tenant-caps:list` now rejects a malformed pagination cursor and unsupported or repeated filters with a validation error instead of returning a wrong page or silently ignoring the filter, and loads per-tenant usage in parallel. The `cap-counter` operator list is no longer searchable, because search resolved against the caller's own tenant instead of all tenants.

title: Unlimited caps show a labelled usage count
detail: The cap usage bar labels an unlimited cap as "<used> · unlimited" through the new `cap-overview.unlimited` key instead of a bare number. The German and Spanish catalogs ship the translation.

title: Cap limits can come from runtime config
detail: `CapSpec.limit(tier, { config })` may return a Promise and gets the caller's config accessor, so a SystemAdmin-editable config key can drive a tier's limit shown by caps:usage and tenant-caps:list. tier-engine's `capsForTier` and cap-counter's `createStockCapGuard` resolver receive the same `{ config }` context (`CapLimitContext`), so enforcement can read the same key. Sync implementations keep working; use system-scoped keys for tier-wide limits.

title: caps:usage declares escapeHatch again so raw-SQL cap providers work
detail: fw#2971 un-exported withUnsafeRawGrant, the mechanism app-owned CapSpec.usage() providers used (via caps:usage's system-mode db) to run raw SQL for aggregates TenantDb has no typed helper for (a SUM, unlike the COUNT(*)-only TenantDb.count() added in fw#2854). caps:usage's own defineQueryHandler(...) call now carries `escapeHatch: { reason: "..." }`, restoring the grant through the same mechanism every other handler-owned unsafeRaw use goes through. Cap providers that only need COUNT(*) should migrate to TenantDb.count(table, where) instead — it needs no escapeHatch at all.

title: CapSpec.limit can now return null for an unlimited usage meter.
detail: A CapSpec's `limit(tier)` may now return `null` to mean unlimited: the cap is still counted (used shows the raw count) but never capped, has no percent, and renders no progress bar or badge. This is a distinct meaning from `limit <= 0`, which unchanged still means 'not part of this tier' and renders as 0/0%.

title: Add cap-overview feature: tier + cap usage visibility per tenant.
detail: New read-only bundled feature. SystemAdmin gets a paged, searchable tenant list with tier/billing columns and per-cap usage bars, plus a per-tenant dashboard reachable from the list. TenantAdmin gets a 'My usage' dashboard showing their own tenant's cap usage as cards. Reads tier-engine, billing-foundation and tenant projections plus caller-supplied CapSpec usage callbacks; every handler enforces explicit tenant scoping (no ambient tenant filter, cross-tenant reads require SystemAdmin + acknowledgeCrossTenant).
